en.title: SNL's GTA 6 vs. Zelda Skit Sparks Fan Debate Over Game Representation
en.summary: Saturday Night Live's latest Weekend Update segment pitted the protagonists of Grand Theft Auto VI and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake against each other. The skit, featuring live-action versions of Jason and Link, humorously debated which game offered a superior experience, igniting conversations among fans.
en.body:
The gaming world is abuzz, not with a new trailer or a surprise announcement, but with a skit from **Saturday Night Live's** Weekend Update. The iconic sketch show recently featured a segment that brought together two of the most anticipated video game releases: **Grand Theft Auto VI** and **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake**. The bit saw live-action interpretations of **GTA VI's** protagonist, Jason (played by Marcello Hernández), and **The Legend of Zelda's** enduring hero, Link (portrayed by Mikey Day), engaging in a comedic clash over whose game reigns supreme.

The skit, which aired on October 3, 2026, was part of a larger discussion on the massive gaming releases dominating November 2026. While many titles have strategically avoided launching alongside the behemoth that is **GTA VI**, Nintendo's **Ocarina of Time remake** stands as a notable exception. The humor in the SNL segment seemingly revolved around the contrasting themes of the two games, with references to car theft and open-world chaos for Jason, and puzzle-solving and adventuring in Hyrule for Link. Weekend Update hosts Colin Jost and Michael Che also participated, adding their own brand of commentary.

## The Digital Duel on Live TV

The premise itself, placing these two distinct gaming icons in conversation, tapped into the ongoing discourse among players about the sheer scale and anticipation surrounding these titles. The fact that **GTA VI** and **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake** are set to be massive, yet fundamentally different, experiences for players is a testament to the diverse landscape of modern gaming. SNL's attempt to capture this rivalry, even in jest, brought the conversation from online forums and social media onto a much broader, mainstream stage. The skit leaned into well-known tropes associated with both franchises, aiming for a relatable humor for a wide audience, though the reception among hardcore fans proved to be a mixed bag.

## Fan Reactions and Representation

As is often the case when popular culture intersects with passionate fanbases, the **SNL** skit has generated considerable discussion online. While some viewers appreciated the nod to the gaming community and the clever juxtaposition of **GTA VI** and **Zelda**, others felt the portrayal, particularly of Jason, missed the mark. Critics pointed to the character's limited engagement with **Grand Theft Auto's** core elements, suggesting a superficial understanding. The joke from Colin Jost, "Now, I don't know much about gaming because I've had sex," also drew varied reactions, highlighting the ongoing challenge of capturing gaming culture accurately for a general audience. Ultimately, the skit served as a humorous, albeit imperfect, reflection of the immense cultural footprint these games have already made.

What's Next

With both **Grand Theft Auto VI** and **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake** slated for release in November 2026, the real-world competition for players' attention and wallets is about to begin. It remains to be seen how these major titles will truly stack up against each other in the eyes of gamers worldwide.

content_raw: Saturday Night Live weighed in on GTA 6 vs. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake with a new Weekend Update skit featuring video game protagonists Jason Duval and Link. Gaming fans were probably surprised to see two of November's biggest releases represented in SNL Season 52. The bit starred live-action versions of GTA 6's Jason and The Legend of Zelda's Link, played by Marcello Hernández and Mikey Day, respectively, and mostly saw the two icons arguing about who has the better game. Also starring Weekend Update hosts Colin Jost and Michael Che, the six-minute video game skit laid it on thick with references to stealing cars, buying RPGs, and solving puzzles in the kingdom of Hyrule. You can see the SNL Weekend Update segment in question below. The protagonists from Legend of Zelda and GTA6 stop by the Update desk pic.twitter.com/19fsg7desg — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) October 4, 2026 The SNL episode was hosted by Verity star Dakota Johnson with musical guest Turnstile and even featured a surprise cameo from pop music mega-star Taylor Swift. The long-running celebrity skit show is no stranger to nights like this, and although it's been known to feature the odd gaming reference here and there , it's safe to say full-on appearances from Link and Jason probably weren't on anyone's bingo card. So, how did this go over with gaming fans? Well… It's not great. "Now, I don't know much about gaming because I've had sex," Jost opened the bit, joking, "but I'm told that people are calling your releases the 'Barbenheimer of video games.'" pic.twitter.com/lI1PCiEOqg — Rampage (@RR4mpage) October 4, 2026 GTA 6 fans say Hernández's Jason leaves much to be desired, with his references to Grand Theft Auto most limited to waving around an RPG and stealing lots and lots of cars. The outfit that helped him bring Jason to life, meanwhile, is little more than a bloody bandage and a tropical button-up. While this Jason falls more into the last-minute Halloween-costume category, Day's Link getup has received praise for being shockingly accurate to the character's specific Ocarina of Time remake tunic. It had some of the same specific details, too, and even came with elf ears and a convincing-enough wig. The jokes, however, didn't land quite as well, and mostly involved Link yelling about puzzles and arguing that his tunic is not a dress. "I'm somebody who still watches SNL most weeks but this sketch was pretty rough," one fan online said . "Basically all of the jokes here were ones I've already been hearing for like 20 years." "Aren't these the same jokes we've heard about Zelda since 2000?" another added . Comment by from discussion in GTA6 I was simply stunned by this: how unending it was, that old ass “people who play video games never have been laid” joke, a complete disregard for specificity in service of surface level nonsense, the middle school talent show presentation. Utterly baffling. — That Week In SNL (@ThatWeekInSNL) October 4, 20
